issues.legal_issue: A landlord seeking eviction from a non-residential business premises must establish that the premises are genuinely required for the landlord’s or a family member’s use.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction from a non-residential premises, claiming that a family member needed it to carry on a business conducted elsewhere.
The tenant disputed that the claimed requirement was bona fide.
The High Court held that proof of bona fide requirement was unnecessary, although it found the landlord’s claim bona fide.
issues.conclusion: A landlord seeking eviction under section 10(3)(a)(iii) must establish bona fide requirement in addition to the other ingredients of that provision; the decision allowing eviction was set aside and the case remanded for reconsideration.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 10(3)(a)(iii) and 10(3)(e) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960, read in context and harmoniously, require proof that the landlord genuinely needs the non-residential premises for the landlord’s or a family member’s use. The words concerning the landlord’s requirement in section 10(3)(a)(ii) must be read into section 10(3)(a)(iii); the requirement that the landlord’s claim be bona fide under section 10(3)(e) concerns the genuineness of that need. This construction accords with the Act’s purpose of preventing unreasonable eviction and distributing buildings equitably. The Court relied on Phiroze Bamanji Desai v. Chandrakant M. Patel and Mattulal v. Radhe Lal on bona fide need, and on Moti Ram v. Suraj Bhan, Neta Ram v. Jiwan Lal, Seaford Court Estates Ltd. v. Asher, M. Pentiah v. Muddala Veeramallappa, and Bangalore Water-Supply & Sewerage Board v. R. Rajappa in addressing construction and the need for bona fide grounds. Mahalakshmi Metal Industries v. K. Suseeladevi, M. Abdul Rahman v. S. Sadasivam, and A. Khan Mohammed v. P. Narayanan Nambiar were overruled.

rule.if: landlord_eviction_petition and nonresidential_business_premises and not vehicle_storage_premises and landlord_or_family_lacks_own_local_business_premises and landlord_seeks_business_occupation

predicates.landlord_eviction_petition: A landlord applies to recover possession of premises from a tenant.
predicates.nonresidential_business_premises: The premises sought are non-residential premises of a kind used for business.
predicates.vehicle_storage_premises: The premises are used or adapted for keeping a vehicle.
predicates.landlord_or_family_lacks_own_local_busin: The landlord or a family member carrying on the business does not occupy an owned non-residential premises for that business in the relevant locality.
predicates.landlord_seeks_business_occupation: The landlord claims that the premises are needed for the landlord’s or a family member’s business use.
predicates.landlord_must_prove_bona_fide_need: The landlord must establish a genuine need for the premises for the landlord’s or a family member’s use.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction from non-residential business premises other than vehicle-storage premises, relies on the absence of an owned local business premises, and seeks possession for business use, the landlord must prove a genuine need for that use.
